Hi Rafael,

We're starting the procurement review for our upcoming rollout and need a set of artifacts to satisfy our legal and security teams. Can Redwood provide the following by May 6:  

1) A certified dataflow map (PDF) showing all hops for Customer Data for the HealthCo integration, explicitly indicating that data processing and backups remain in the EU.
2) A technical VPC architecture diagram that explains network egress controls and routing policies.
3) A short attestation letter stating Redwood will process HealthCo customer data in EU-only infrastructure (no cross-border processing) and specify key management location and ownership.
4) Confirmation of applicable standards: SOC 2 Type II report availability, SIG/CAIQ evidence, and whether Redwood will accept SCCs (or provide equivalent DPA language).
5) Clarification on HIPAA scope: if HealthCo elects to store PHI, what additional controls or boundary scoping (DPIA) Redwood requires and whether Redwood will sign any HIPAA-specific addendum.

We're on a tight procurement timeline. If possible, please include a draft attestation we can share with legal. Happy to set a 30-min call next week to go through technical questions.

Thanks,
Elena Varga
Head of Security Procurement
HealthCo GmbH

Rafael / Marissa —

We can meet HealthCo's ask. Attached are the artifacts I prepared: dataflow_map_v2.pdf (canonical customer-data flow), vpc_architecture_diagram.png, and a draft attestation_letter_draft.pdf. Short tech summary below that we should include in the attestation and share with procurement:  

- Regional routing: Redwood uses policy-based routing at the edge to pin requests to regional inference pools. For HealthCo we will configure an EU-only routing policy that prevents any requests from being routed to non-EU model pools.
- VPC deployment: For Private customers we deploy a dedicated VPC in the requested cloud region (EU-West). The VPC is isolated, with egress controls limited to our EU NAT gateways (EU CIDR ranges). Cross-region replication is disabled by default for customer data; any replication requires explicit customer agreement.
- Key management: Options: (1) Customer-managed KMS keys (recommended) located in the customer's EU KMS project; (2) Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys stored in EU region. Both options keep key material within EU boundaries.
- Backups & logs: Backups for Private deployments are stored in EU-only storage buckets by configuration. Audit logs are retained in our EU logging cluster; however, support access is via our control plane which can be configured to route to the customer's private control plane (for Private deployments).
- Certifications/evidence: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and CAIQ/SIG condensed answers are available from the compliance portal. I'll include links.

Attachments: dataflow_map_v2.pdf (application/pdf - stub), vpc_architecture_diagram.png (image/png - stub), attestation_letter_draft.pdf (application/pdf - stub), dpa_scc_clause_redwood.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document - stub)

- Marissa: send these to Elena and ask whether they want a signed PDF or a notarized letter.

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the clear list. Please find attached the artifacts we discussed:

- dataflow_map_v2.pdf (canonical dataflow map for HealthCo integration)
- vpc_architecture_diagram.png (technical VPC diagram showing egress controls and regional routing)
- attestation_letter_draft.pdf (draft attestation we can sign)
- dpa_scc_clause_redwood.docx (DPA with SCCs clause for review)

Key points (summary):
- EU-only routing: We will configure a customer-specific EU-only routing policy which pins inference requests and persistent storage to EU model pools and storage endpoints. This is enforced at the edge and at the serving layer; fallback to non-EU pools will not occur for pinned customers.
- Key management: We recommend customer-managed KMS keys in their EU account. If they choose Redwood-managed keys, keys will be HSM-backed and stored in the EU region.
- Backups & logs: For Private deployments backups and audit logs are stored in EU-only buckets/ logging clusters by default. No cross-border replication unless explicitly enabled via contract addendum.
- Certifications: SOC 2 Type II report and CAIQ/SIG summary are available in our compliance portal; I'll provide links via a secure share if you want them.
- HIPAA: If HealthCo stores PHI with Redwood, we'll need a HIPAA addendum. We can support HIPAA workloads in Private deployments with scoped controls; we recommend a short DPIA to enumerate processing of PHI.

Attached are the drafts; please review and let us know:  (1) if the attestation wording needs changes (you mentioned 'no egress to US' as a desired phrase), and (2) whether you require notarization or the signed PDF is sufficient.

We can jump on a 30-min call if helpful — I am available Thursday morning (Europe time).

Best,

Rafael / Neha / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. The materials look useful. A couple of clarifications before we close procurement:  

1) Backups: please confirm backups are stored only in EU and whether there are any short-term snapshots replicated to other regions for durability reasons. We need an explicit line in the attestation about backup residency.
2) Audit logs & support access: please confirm audit logs and any historical request traces are stored in EU-only storage and whether Redwood support access could ever route through US-based infrastructure.

If you can add the sentence "Redwood will not transfer, replicate, or permit egress of HealthCo Customer Data to any location outside the EU without prior written consent" to the attestation and re-send a signed PDF, we can proceed. We do not require notarization at this stage but legal will want the signed attestation plus the DPA with SCCs.

Also: on HIPAA — HealthCo may classify a subset of data as PHI. Please confirm Redwood's readiness to sign a HIPAA addendum for Private deployments and the rough timeline (we need to know if this will delay go-live).

Appreciate it — once we have the updated attestation and the DPA + SOC 2 link, we can move to signatures on our side.
